newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares slump on lifeless market.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares slump on lifeless market.

text.p: Danish share prices slumped on Thursday in a fairly dull market, with dealers seeing nothing to reverse the trend on Friday.
"Trade was somewhat thin and the market is generally flat at the moment," a dealer said, adding that falls were spread fairly evenly over the top 20 stocks with none standing out in particular.

The KFX top-20 index closed 0.34 point down, at 165.51, in overall bourse turnover of 1.14 million crowns. The KFX June future fell 0.45 point, to 164.90, with 247 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
"I can't see anything that could correct the tendency for falls, so I think we will slip again tomorrow," the dealer said.
Sophus Berendsen was likely to be the object of attention on Friday in the wake of its announcement, after Thursday's bourse close, that it intended to split into two separately-listed companies.

One would hold most of the firm's 35.8 percent stake in Britain's Rentokil Initial and the other would own the group's remaining activities, Berendsen said. Berendsen closed at 889.00 crowns, 0.9 crown up from Wednesday's close.
